title: Seabright Logistics outbound raw notes
body:
Context / why this matters:
- Seabright Logistics: mid-size 3PL, 1500 employees, strong East Coast coverage, experimenting with automation for customer support + rate quoting.
- Potential fit: Redwood inference for (a) automated quoting assistant integrated into their TMS, (b) chat-based customer status queries, (c) reranking returns candidates for cheapest/faster lanes.
- Key impetus: reduce manual quoting time (avg 18 min now), reduce inbound CS tickets for ETA/exception questions, and standardize carrier selection logic.

Quick account snapshot (notes from call 2025-11-06):
- Contacted via intro from Chris at ChannelPartners.
- Decision maker: Priya Nair (Head of Product) - previously built internal ML infra.
- Influencer: Marco Diaz (Ops Director) - cares about throughput and predictability.
- Procurement: standard RFP for tech vendors Q1 2026.
- Current stack: Cloud-hosted TMS (FreightFlex), internal rule engine, small in-house NLU for intent classification (Spacy-based).
- Constraint: security + SOC2 required, can't send PHI/SSN offsite without encryption controls.

Primary pain points they verbalized:
- Manual quoting backlog during peak windows (Mon-Tue mornings).
- Inaccurate ETAs from carriers leading to CS escalations.
- Poor visibility: teams copy/paste notes between systems.
- Cost sensitivity: procurement wants cost model aligned to per-request economics.

Value props to emphasize (internal checklist):
- Predictable latency + batching to avoid fail-on-load spikes (Dedicated/reserved capacity).
- Private deployment option for sensitive metadata (VPC/on-prem).
- Cost controls: quantization + caching to lower per-token unit cost.
- Observability: per-route latency/cost metrics to map to carrier selection rules.

Outbound cadence (proposed):
- Touch 0: LinkedIn InMail to Priya (short, reference Chris, one-liner use case).
- Touch 1 (email 1): problem + 15-min exploratory meeting ask + suggested times.
- Touch 2 (call): discovery script (see below).
- Touch 3 (email follow-up): one-pager + small pilot outline for a 6-week POC.
- Touch 4 (handshake): intro to Solutions Eng + security lead, provide SOC2 + data flow diagram.

Cold email draft (short):
Subject: Reduce quoting backlog at Seabright by 40% in 6 weeks
Hi Priya —
Spoke to Chris at ChannelPartners and thought I should reach out. Redwood helps logistics teams automate quote generation and routable carrier selection while keeping cost predictable (dedicated capacity + caching).
Would a 15-minute chat next week make sense? I can walk through a 6-week pilot plan we ran with Harborline that cut manual quote time by ~45%.
Best,
Maya

Voicemail / call openers (short scripts):
- "Hey Priya, it’s Maya from Redwood — quick check if reducing manual quoting is still a top priority this quarter? I have a 15-min demo plan to show speed and economics."
- If gatekeeper: "We’re proposing a 6-week pilot (non-invasive) that shows token-level cost + latency before any commit. Need Priya & Marco for 30 mins to align."

Discovery call checklist (questions + red flags):
- How many quotes per day/week? (red flag: <100/day -> may not justify dedicated)
- Current SLA for quoting latency (target vs actual).
- What data must never leave their network? (PII/PHI/SSN)
- Are there existing rate tables/APIs from carriers? (integration complexity)
- Who owns the routing logic? (ops vs product vs procurement)
- Success criteria for a pilot? (time saved, reduced tickets, cost per quote)
- Budget cadence and procurement windows (Q1 2026 RFP noted).

Common objections & suggested rebuttals (short-hand):
- "We can't send customer data to third party." -> "We offer Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) + KMS integrations; we can do field redaction in the POC and run on dedicated capacity for the pilot."
- "Cost unpredictable / per-token billing concern." -> "Pilot uses reserved capacity + controlled batch settings to model unit economics; we can provide sample cost breakdown from similar workload (see Harborline case)."
- "We already built something in house." -> "Cool — product teams usually run into maintenance and scale regressions; we can run a drop-in evaluation to compare throughput/latency and ops overhead in 2 weeks."
- "Security sign-off takes months." -> "Offer to start with a low-risk non-prod integration (read-only) and share SOC2 + technical design early. Also propose a short security Q&A with their SecOps."

Pilot outline (6 weeks, low friction):
- Week 0: kickoff + dataflow review (2 hrs).
- Week 1: ingest sample quoting logs, map input/output schema (SE + Data Eng).
- Week 2: small inference pipeline in Redwood hosted sandbox (no PII) + latency baseline.
- Week 3-4: integrate with staging TMS for automated quoting in subset of accounts (1 region).
- Week 5: measure KPIs (quotes/min, avg latency, ticket volume delta).
- Week 6: review + next steps (dedicated capacity quote / private deployment options).

Success metrics to commit to on pilot (examples):
- Reduce avg quote time from 18 min -> <8 min for >70% of requests.
- Keep  p95 latency for generation < 1500ms in staging traffic profile.
- Show cost-per-quote and projected monthly spend under reserved capacity scenario.
- Demonstrate integration path for ETA enrichment + reranking.

Materials to prepare (todo):
- One-pager customized for Seabright with estimated cost ranges (Evan).
- Example dataflow diagram + privacy controls (Riley).
- Harborline case study redacted (legal ok?) — use as precedent.
- Short demo script: live quote generator + token cost breakdown (sandbox).

Notes to self / quick reminders:
- Priya likes concrete numbers — lead with time-saved and cost per quote.
- Marco will push for ops simplicity — emphasize turnkey connectors and autoscaling policies.
- Procurement timeline: be ready for dec/Jan follow-up; propose pilot start in late Jan.
- Keep it tight: 15-30 min initial call, demo only if 2 stakeholders present.

Linked references / signals:
- LinkedIn: Priya Nair - posts about ML infra.
- Mentioned competitors: Custom in-house NLU; current vendors (CarrierSync API).
- Channel intro: Chris @ ChannelPartners (email thread id: slack thread #channel-intros).

Open questions / unknowns (for research):
- Exact quote volume distribution by lane/sku (need sample log).
- Which fields are considered "sensitive" by Seabright SecOps (they may call carrier account numbers sensitive).
- Willingness to sign an NDA before sending sample logs?

Next steps (immediate):
- Send short intro email + propose 3 time slots (Maya) — target next Tue/Thu mornings.
- Prep cost one-pager and sandbox demo sample (Evan) by Thu 11/13.
- Schedule 30-min internal sync with SE + Security to align on redaction plan (Riley + Maya).

Rough outreach templates (for iteration):
- Social touch script: "Congrats on the growth Priya — saw Seabright expanded East Hub network. Curious how you’re thinking about automating quoting at scale?"
- Cold DM: "We helped a 3PL cut manual quotes by ~45% in 6 weeks without sending PII to third parties — would love 10 mins to see if that fits."

Misc scratch/fragments:
- "ask about peak windows (Mon 08:00-11:00)"
- "prep a trade-off table: hosted vs dedicated vs private with rough cost bands"
- "check if they use EDI 214 for tracking -> could feed into ETA model"
- "Marco cares about circuit breaker for fallbacks"

End of doc — quick iteration log:
- 2025-11-08 initial capture after intro call.
- 2025-11-10 internal notes added (Evan).
- 2025-11-15 cleaned up outreach sequence and pilot bulleted plan.
